newsitem.title: UK: CWS tells SFO of concerns about Regan firm payment.
newsitem.headline: CWS tells SFO of concerns about Regan firm payment.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS) said on Tuesday it had drawn the attention of the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) to its concerns about a payment in a deal between the CWS and a company controlled by entrepreneur Andrew Regan.

"We have now formally drawn this situation to the attention of the SFO," a spokesman told Reuters, adding this related to unsatisfactory replies it had received to requests for explanations from Regan. But an SFO official said it was not investigating the affair.
The court order followed the suspension last week of two senior CWS executives, Allan Green and David Chambers, for an alleged serious breach of trust.

The order prohibited Regan, his company Lanica Trust offshoot company Galileo, Lanica director and former CWS adviser David Lyons and Green from using any confidential material they may have about the CWS.

Regan has written to CWS chairman Melmoth in reply to questions about an earlier deal bewteen CWS and Hobson, a company then run by Regan. In the letter, he said a payment queried by Melmoth formed part of a legitimate transaction, which had been in the best interests of Hobson.

Regan's Galileo was last week about to bid over one billion pounds ($1.6 billion) for the non-retail parts CWS, which include the profitable Co-operative Bank, with the intention of breaking the business up. Buyers have already emerged for some of the businesses.
